directChecks.independentGeometryAlgorithm: For each PCB trace, consecutive wire points on the same layer define planar segments. Segments <= 1e-8 mm are metadata duplicates and ignored. Calculate atan2 angle and deviation from nearest multiple of 45 degrees; report >0.1 degree. Compare adjacent same-layer nonzero segments at common endpoints for turns >135.1 degrees. Compare nonadjacent segments on a common layer for interior centerline intersections or positive collinear centerline overlaps using cross products; 1e-8 mm intersection tolerance.
directChecks.shortSegmentsDisposition: These short finite segments are endpoint/head artifacts, not automatically poor routing or clearance violations. No deduction for them without evidence that contacts can safely be simplified.

strengths: Fresh official style check is empty, independently confirmed by the exact capture angle scan.
No immediate near reversal or nonadjacent same-trace interior crossing/centerline overlap found across 633 traces.
Declared controlled widths, true source endpoints and physical routing boundaries have explicit archived evidence rather than treating angle lint as DRC.
The prior exact-capture connectivity receipt claims 450/450 joins; this review independently verifies geometry style, not that full contact classification.

findings.explanation: The protected fan feed takes a large perimeter route. This is a solid but long power route and prevents an exceptional economy score. Shortening is a candidate for an obstacle-aware experiment; the straight endpoint distance is not a legal route proof.

INPUT_FAULT_N has 14 nonzero segments over 30.245 mm while its endpoints are 13.884 mm apart. It changes direction through several 0.25 mm steps near its destination. This is a clear routing polish target even though it passes angle lint; feasibility of a shorter replacement has not been established.

UART_TX header path is 56.079 mm with 12 segments for 31.546 mm endpoint span. UART_RX bottom trunk is similarly indirect. These low-speed lines are not blockers on this evidence, but reducing bends and perimeter travel would improve the routing.

Two top-layer fan feedback/compensation segments each exceed twice the endpoint span. Their route shape includes a long vertical side corridor around resistor locations. This deserves compact-placement and legal-path review, particularly since feedback nodes benefit from compact geometry. No noise failure is demonstrated.

The archived actual whole R206 path has only 0.05 mm margin under its declared bound. It passes, but this bound is sensitive to route edits. This is a maintenance concern, not proof the path is electrically too long.

suspectedShortAssessment.status: not determined by this style scope
suspectedShortAssessment.explanation: Style lint verifies angle/route-shape properties and cannot decide whether different-net copper on a common layer overlaps. I found no self-loop crossings within individual traces, but that result does not exclude foreign-net overlaps, traces against pours, pads or via barrels. The image crop must be mapped to coordinates and copper/net layers by the geometry review roles.

topImprovements: Prioritize an obstacle-aware shorter fan feed while maintaining its 0.8 mm width, safe returns and layer clearances.
Simplify INPUT_FAULT_N and UART bottom trunks while preserving proven physical contacts.
Compare fan feedback placement and routing against a compact alternative; validate actual obstacles before editing.
Keep copper clearance and foreign-net overlap results separate from style-lint results.
limitations: No source, circuit, runtime, or existing review edits; no builds or autorouting.
The CLI checker unexpectedly auto-wrote checks/check-pcb-style/pcb.svg under the project despite no --svg flag. Reported this immediately to parent; circuit SHA stayed exact.
Score measures style/economy and stated evidence; it is not a manufacturing, EMI, thermal, SI or bench readiness rating.
Detour ratios use obstacle-ignoring endpoint distances; they identify candidates rather than proving legal shortcuts.
No exhaustive foreign-net copper DRC performed in this assigned role.
